decisions.note: Locator 47:100701211 is verified as JP エクストリーム下校術; the Vietnamese title keeps the deliberately exaggerated 'extreme going-home technique' joke without importing an English localization.

Locator 47:201582 is verified as JP 究極のヒルクライマー, but natural Vietnamese title choices such as 'tay leo dốc', 'nhà leo dốc' and a more honorific phrasing differ materially; defer rather than freeze an awkward label.
Locator 47:105001211 is verified as JP 駆り立てる想い. The emotional noun 想い and the driving/urging nuance admit several literary Vietnamese renderings, so a canonical title should receive style review.

Locator 47:102201211 is verified as JP 天空落とし. It is a stylized technique name, and literal Vietnamese versus a compact Sino-Vietnamese title would create noticeably different tone; defer for consistent skill-name style.

Locator 47:200521 is verified as JP 空回り. The Japanese is idiomatic ('spinning one's wheels'/fruitless overexertion), while the Chinese bridge is more literal; defer rather than lock a misleading mechanical calque.

Locator 47:101103111 is verified as JP 射貫く蒼. The elliptical 蒼 can denote an azure/blue image without naming a concrete object, so Vietnamese choices that add 'trời' or another noun would be interpretive; defer.
Locator 47:111101 is verified as JP 時かけるせせらぎ. This compact poetic title relies on wordplay around time and a murmuring stream; multiple natural Vietnamese literary phrasings remain defensible.
Locator 47:202381 is verified as JP ブレイクスルー; 'Đột phá' is the established natural Vietnamese equivalent of the loanword concept.

Locator 47:203571 is verified as JP 突破口. A Vietnamese lock must stay distinct from 47:202381 ブレイクスルー ('Đột phá'); choices such as 'cửa đột phá', 'điểm mở' or 'kẽ hở' need terminology-level consistency review.
